speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how many days ago you delivered your baby and how high your fever has gotten?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. I'd like to examine your abdomen to assess the extent of the tenderness and check for any masses. Can you tell me if you have had any chills or night sweats since delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the uterine discharge have a foul odor, and have you noticed any redness or swelling at the site of your urinary catheterization? I need to differentiate between endometritis and a urinary tract infection.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Uncomplicated pregnancy leading up to a vaginal delivery. No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: Does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. Lives with her partner.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify the nature of your uterine discharge to better assess for infection. Is the lochia foul-smelling, and have you experienced any chills or rigors?

speaker: Patient
text: Complains of minor difficulty in breathing but denies any urinary pain, headache, vomiting, or diarrhea.

speaker: Doctor
text: The minor difficulty in breathing is concerning, so I need to rule out a pulmonary embolism or other complications. I will order some tests to check your blood counts and imaging to assess your lungs and abdomen. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Chest_X-Ray, Pelvic_Ultrasound
